authorization_decision.required_successor: immutable superseding r7-or-later runner, authorization schema, tests, zero-fit seal, two deterministic preflights, and fresh independent QA

findings.title: The normal parent flow does not hold the complete private snapshot or runtime closure across import
evidence: The sealed static snapshot has 51 entries and the execution snapshot has 54 after authorization, seal, and QA are added.
scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v6.py:3571-3586 holds only seven private-snapshot paths: the runner plus authorization, seal, QA, design, execution module, and v5 trust amendment.

scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v6.py:3243-3261 brackets project imports with exact-tree checks, but the remaining legacy runner and transitive project sources are reopened without deny-write/delete handles between those checks.

scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v6.py:1057-1161 prechecks only METADATA and top-level entrypoints for 12 distributions. The sealed receipt reports 1213 loaded runtime files, but their aggregate is computed only after import by scripts/run_p1_round_b_nonspike_long_event_residual_v1r6.py:936-1019.
The LightGBM native library and the Python executable are authenticated after they have already been loaded or started; post-execution hashing is evidence, not a pre-execution trust boundary.
attack_path: Wait until the worker completes its first exact snapshot check.
Replace an unheld transitive project source or pure-Python runtime dependency, allow import-time code to execute, and restore the sealed bytes before the second check or post-import aggregate.
Both later digests can match even though untrusted code already executed before the claim and can mutate state or perform scientific work outside the ledger.
findings.impact: The r5 arbitrary-code-before-authentication class remains open below the now-correct isolated bootstrap, so the package is not safely authorizable.
required_fix: Hold deny-write/delete handles over every executable/transitive private-snapshot file from final verification through worker termination, not only seven authorities.

Seal a full per-path runtime inventory including Python sources, extension modules, native libraries, and loaded dependencies; verify and hold each before any import or LoadLibrary and retain the handles through worker termination.
Recheck exact loaded-module/native membership after import and immediately before claim as defense in depth.

findings.title: The directly callable hidden worker accepts a caller-authenticated manifest and caller-selected runtime search roots
evidence: scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v6.py:3642-3677 exposes --worker with caller-supplied manifest hash, bootstrap hash, deadline, and the externally readable authorization digest.

scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v6.py:2509-2528 places strict_readiness in a parent-created manifest, but scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v6.py:2652-2811 never binds that object back to the seal's readonly_preflight_verification_sha256 or sealed runtime receipt.
scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v6.py:3231-3242 activates explicit runtime search paths from that caller-supplied strict_readiness before numerical imports.
scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v6.py:3202-3216 compares post-import readiness only with the same caller-supplied manifest object.
attack_path: After a valid authorization exists, copy the sealed snapshot authorities and create a manifest whose self-declared runtime inventory points at an attacker-controlled import root.
Pass the digest of that manifest on the hidden-worker command line; there is no parent-only secret or seal-bound manifest digest.
The worker verifies the attacker's self-consistent metadata and top-level hashes, inserts the root, and executes its imports before any fixed aggregate mismatch can stop it.
findings.impact: A valid external authorization does not constrain the worker to the sealed runtime readiness, allowing arbitrary pre-claim code execution despite correct -I -S -B bootstrap flags.
required_fix: Bind the exact canonical manifest or strict-readiness digest, runtime inventory digest, canonical output root, and deadline policy into the seal and external authorization.
Require an unforgeable single-use parent capability or acquire the canonical one-shot claim before accepting any worker-controlled manifest field.
Reject every worker manifest whose canonical readiness digest differs from the sealed preflight authority before activating a search path.

findings.title: Hidden-worker replay can bypass the canonical lifetime attempt and hard-wall boundaries
evidence: scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v6.py:2509-2526 records output_project_root only in the self-created manifest, not in the seal or authorization.
scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v6.py:2562-2580 accepts any existing absolute root with the fixed relative artifact suffix rather than the canonical repository root.
scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v6.py:3176-3182 considers a copied seal under each alternate root a clean one-shot namespace.
The hidden --deadline-epoch is caller supplied and is checked only for expiry at scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v6.py:3262-3263.
findings.impact: The same future authorization can be replayed into multiple alternate roots, repeating the 72 fits and 21 materializations and selecting an arbitrarily distant deadline.
required_fix: Bind and exactly verify the resolved canonical repository/output identity in the seal and authorization.
Bind the fixed deadline derivation and parent supervision capability, and make the authorization digest consumable exactly once in the canonical namespace.

findings.title: Duplicate JSON keys are collapsed before the claimed exact authorization-schema check
evidence: scripts/run_p1_long_event_segment_proposal_rescore_v6.py:366-438 checks the resulting mapping's key sets and types, so duplicate top-level or nested wire keys have already been silently reduced to one value.
Focused negative tests cover wrong version, missing, extra, and wrong-type fields but not duplicate object keys.
findings.impact: No independent privilege bypass is needed for the P0 verdict, but the promised exact raw authorization schema is not literally enforced.
required_fix: Parse authorization, seal, QA, and manifest JSON with recursive duplicate-key rejection before semantic validation.
Add duplicate top-level and nested-key negative tests that fail before any static read, import, snapshot, or claim.
